The gain did not generalize: 7 dev cases are too few. Deferred until the eval has enough labelled cases.

entries.name: SkyPilot
entries.description: The AI Compute Platform: runs AI workloads across clouds and GPU providers, with a cost optimizer, managed jobs and auto-stop.
entries.license_status: open source; no code copied (ideas and API shapes only)
entries.agent_os_overlap: quote.py prices options from explicit inputs; no provisioning or live GPU catalog yet (IMP-0015 Phase 2).
entries.integration: none now; borrow catalog shape and optimizer/auto-stop semantics for the RunPod adapter; spike SkyPilot as an optional provisioning backend before Phase 2 lifecycle work

risks.dependency_weight: heavy (many cloud SDKs, its own state/API server)

evidence.development_savings: large if adopted for provisioning; small now
evidence.runtime_savings: its optimizer targets the same API-vs-GPU choice
evidence.security: credentials live in its own config; would need secret_refs bridging

entries.rationale: The closest prior art for the Compute Broker: price catalogs, cheapest-feasible placement, auto-stop and preemption recovery. Too heavy to embed in the stdlib runtime for the read-only quote slice. Borrow its catalog and optimizer semantics now, and spike it as an optional provisioning backend (WRAP candidate) before implementing pod lifecycle in-house. 2026-09-30: an in-house RunPod pod lifecycle now exists (budget-metered, reaper, crash handling), so the 'spike before in-house lifecycle' step is superseded; SkyPilot stays the reference for catalogs/placement and becomes a WRAP candidate only if a second GPU cloud (e.g. Vast.ai, whose public offers API was checked) is needed.
provenance: documented project scope; no code spike yet
revisit_when: a second GPU cloud is needed
multi-cloud failover for capacity errors is required

entries.name: vLLM
entries.description: A high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs.
entries.license_status: open source; no code copied (ideas and API shapes only)
entries.agent_os_overlap: adapters/http_api.OpenAiCompatibleAdapter already targets OpenAI-compatible servers by base_url; orchestrate model-add registers them.
entries.integration: external process only: the recommended serving engine for self-hosted or abliterated weights on a pod or local GPU; Agent OS talks to it over HTTP with no Python dependency

evidence.runtime_savings: throughput per GPU-hour feeds quote.py inputs
evidence.quality: live 2026-09-29/30: served Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct as foreman (planner) and, with --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes, as a Codex CLI coding agent via /v1/responses (task PASSED first attempt)
evidence.reliability: vllm/vllm-openai:latest crash-looped once silently on a community pod (restarts, no API to logs) -> Agent OS wraps it with a crash-log reporter + uptime crash-loop detection; later pods ready in ~3 min
evidence.security: endpoint guarded by VLLM_API_KEY (env, not argv: vLLM logs its args); /metrics is unauthenticated (counts only)
evidence.maintenance: very active; wrapped as an external image, no in-repo dependency
evidence.portability: OpenAI-compatible chat + Responses APIs; YaRN context extension via --hf-overrides works (64k on a 32k-native Qwen2.5)

entries.rationale: The default serving engine to recommend for open-weight and abliterated models: an OpenAI-compatible server the existing adapter already speaks. Wrap it as an external process (local or on a RunPod pod) rather than importing it. Spike done 2026-09-30 (foreman_deploy.py): wrapped as an external process on RunPod pods, pinned revision, crash reporter, metrics sampling; stays WRAP.
provenance: documented project scope; no code spike yet
revisit_when: a served model family needs a tool-call parser not yet mapped

entries.name: Hermes Agent
entries.description: Self-improving personal agent: messaging gateway, bounded memory, self-maintained skills, cron, subagents, plugins and MCP
entries.license_status: MIT; operator granted academic reuse permission 2026-09-29; attribution recorded
entries.agent_os_overlap: Executive function (EXEC-7/11.5/12/13, P2.2) is largely unbuilt in Agent OS and is Hermes' strength. Orchestrator OS already exceeds Hermes for verified multi-agent code work (worktrees, validators, cross-review, gates).

run: one-shot CLI `hermes -z` as an orchestrator worker

risks.churn: commits daily; internal APIs carry no compatibility shims; pin a release and use only CLI, MCP and plugin ABCs
risks.state: one writer per HERMES_HOME; built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md would fork state unless the Agent OS provider plugin is used
risks.spend: Nous Portal/OpenRouter are paid; default to local models under allow_paid_spend=false
risks.exposure: gateway accepts inbound messages; DM pairing + allowlists mandatory; sends stay approval-gated

evidence.development_savings: large for executive function (gateway, cron, voice already built)
evidence.runtime_savings: no-agent cron and deterministic curator avoid model calls; unmeasured in Agent OS
evidence.security: command approval, DM pairing, protected write paths upstream
evidence.complexity: large (~8k Python files); integrate only through stable seams

entries.rationale: Run Hermes as the executive front door (messaging, cron, voice) and as an optional any-model worker, with Agent OS canonical through MCP and a memory-provider plugin; port the curator lifecycle and the fallback wait threshold; borrow its caching and footprint rules. Skip its multi-agent board as a runtime. See the evaluation document for the per-capability split and phased tests (H1-H6).
provenance: local shallow clone of NousResearch/hermes-agent at bd394e2a (2026-10-01): README.md, AGENTS.md, website/docs, hermes_cli/_parser.py, agent/memory_provider.py, mcp_serve.py, gateway/platforms, plugins/platforms
local shallow clone of NousResearch/hermes-agent-self-evolution (2026-10-01): README.md
